To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Graph-Augmented Multi-Modal Deep Learning Framework for Fracture Detection, leveraging the strengths of convolutional and graph-based learning techniques to enhance fracture identification and classification. The proposed model integrates multi-modal medical imaging data (X-rays, CT scans), improving its adaptability across different imaging techniques. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are employed for feature extraction, while Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) model spatial and structural relationships within bone fractures, enabling precise localization and classification, particularly in cases of overlapping, comminuted, and subtle fractures. Additionally, explainable AI (XAI) techniques, such as Grad-CAM and saliency maps, are incorporated to enhance interpretability, providing radiologists with a transparent understanding of AI-driven diagnoses. To streamline clinical workflows, the system generates structured diagnostic reports, detailing fracture type, severity, and localization, ensuring consistency and reducing reporting time. The proposed framework is rigorously evaluated on multi-modal and real-world datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness in improving diagnostic accuracy, reducing human error, and enhancing clinical decision-making. By bridging the gap between AI-driven automation and radiological expertise, this research contributes to the advancement of intelligent medical imaging systems, making fracture diagnosis more efficient, accurate, and accessible in diverse healthcare settings.\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.52783/jes.9147\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2025, 4, 28]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.26434/chemrxiv.15010270/v1\", \"title\": [\"Drug Molecular and Route Similarity-Aware Retrieval-Augmented LLM Generation with Knowledge Graph for Semantic Reasoning\"], \"abstract\": \"To address the inherent limitations of large language models (LLMs) in chemical synthesis—hallucinations, and low knowledge dense—this study presents a Knowledge Graph–enhanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation framework (KG-RAG-LLM) with a multi-scale calculation of molecular and route similarity. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that KG-RAG-LLM significantly mitigates hallucinations, increasing the proportion of concrete chemical information in generated responses to 39.52%–40.87%, drastically outperforming baseline LLMs and standard literature-based RAG pipelines in response completeness and accuracy. To overcome the inability of traditional 2D linear fingerprints to capture 3D spatial properties and reaction path variations, we further developed a multidimensional molecular and route similarity calculation combining SimHash, core similarity, and FCFP, as an alternative to Route CGR representations coupled with UMAP dimensionality reduction. This formulation accurately distinguishes between subtle and distinct synthetic strategies, demonstrating superior precision over traditional clustering methods for fuzzy retrieval of synthetic routes. Overall, this work provides a reliable, knowledge-dense solution for intelligent retrosynthetic Semantic Reasoning.\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.26434/chemrxiv.15010270/v1\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026, 10, 12]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.21203/rs.3.rs-9923118/v1\", \"title\": [\"LLM-Augmented Knowledge Graph Reasoning with Disentangled Multimodal Fusion for Explainable E-Commerce Conversion Predictio\"], \"abstract\": \"Abstract\\n

\\n E-commerce conversion prediction is a foundation of modern recommender systems, yet existing methods often suffer from three intertwined limitations: entangled multimodal representations that mix spurious and causal factors, shallow knowledge-graph reasoning whose attention weights are not faithfully explanatory, and a lack of human-readable rationales suitable for business decision making. We propose\\n LADMF\\n , a unified framework that couples\\n LLM-Augmented Knowledge Graph Reasoning\\n with\\n Disentangled Multimodal Fusion\\n and a\\n Cross-Modal Causal Attention\\n module to address all three limitations in a principled way. Concretely, LADMF first decomposes the joint representation of users and items into modality-shared and modality-specific subspaces under a distance-correlation disentanglement constraint and a mutual-information bottleneck. Second, it enriches a multimodal knowledge graph with LLM-generated semantic triples and re-scores reasoning paths via a frozen LLM acting as an external knowledge prior. Third, it replaces vanilla attention with counterfactual causal attention that computes intervention-aware weights through a do-operator. A purchase-aware contrastive objective and a path-faithfulness loss are introduced to align the prediction with the explanation. Extensive experiments on three public datasets, Amazon-Electronics, Taobao-CTR, and JD-Conversion, demonstrate that LADMF improves AUC by 2.5%–3.4% over the strongest baseline, generates substantially more faithful and plausible explanations under human evaluation, and remains robust under severe sparsity. Code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/Ladmf-548F/.\\n
